newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Motorola pulls out of Ukraine mobile deal.
newsitem.headline: Motorola pulls out of Ukraine mobile deal.

text.p: Motorola Inc is pulling out of a project with a Ukrainian partner which is co-launching a GSM 900 standard mobile phone network in the former Soviet republic, the U.S. telecoms giant told Reuters on Thursday.
"Motorola is stopping its investment project with URS (Ukrainian Radio Systems)," spokeswoman Viktoria Bondar said, adding that Motorola's other activities in Ukraine would continue.
Motorola had invested "several million dollars" in the project. "If the project had come to fruition we were planning to invest half a billion," she said.
But Motorola would continue a string of other activities across Ukraine involving radio and paging systems, she said.
"Motorola's network management group did not think they could continue the work because of the constantly changing conditions of licensing in Ukraine," she said.
The U.S. firm opened a representative office in Ukraine in late 1993 and the GSM project was its biggest project, she said.
Bondar said that Motorola was assisting URS in finding a new partner to continue its activities as one of three firms who won the GSM tender on March 11.
She gave no further details and URS officials were not available for comment.
Foreign investors in Ukraine, particularly in the nascent telecoms sector, have complained about bureaucratic hurdles, demands for bribes and a lack of legislation in the past.
